action: Kurly curators and customers: expect phishing that uses your name, phone or email; Kurly says it will notify the 2 affected general customers individually.
date_note: Dailysecu (21 November) says the external access happened on 17 November; Kurly reported it to the relevant agencies on 18 November and its CEO apologised on 20 November.
exec: A leak of personal data of 10,701 people at a Korean online retailer, including some account and resident or business registration numbers of curators.
geo_basis: country as stated (South Korea); Seoul used as the pin, city not stated in the source
plain: Korean online grocer Kurly says an outside attacker stole credentials and got into internal systems, leaking personal data of 10,701 people, mostly curator-program participants.
summary: Dailysecu reports that Kurly said an external attacker accessed its system by an abnormal method on 17 November, stole credentials and used them to enter internal business systems without authorisation. Kurly told the relevant agencies on 18 November. Its investigation confirmed a leak of personal data of 10,701 people: 10,699 curator-program participants and 2 general customers. For some curators this included account numbers and resident or business registration numbers.
title: Kurly says credentials stolen in 17 November intrusion; personal data of 10,701 people leaked

validation.note: Only Dailysecu (Korean) read; it relays Kurly's own statement (CEO apology of 20 November). Kurly's notice and a second publisher were not read.

review.note: Compared with Dailysecu (21 Nov, relays Kurly statement): 17 Nov access, 18 Nov report, 10,701 = 10,699 curators + 2 customers match. Fixed exec: said ID numbers; source says account and resident or business registration numbers. Single source; Kurly notice not read.
